production: v2.0.1; not accessed or changed during this audit
deployment: HELD — later explicit deploy request required

bugs.reproduction: Open a retained past, unresolved workout from an ended program through Training History.
bugs.expected: History and Calendar expose the same hold and omit forbidden workout/edit actions.
bugs.actual: History omitted programHeld, so the shared page advertised actions rejected by the server.
bugs.root: TrainingHistoryController did not pass the existing ProgramRun::holds result to the shared detail page.
bugs.fix: Pass the hold flag; ensure the shared Resume action also respects it.

bugs.reproduction: Pause a program from 5 November, advance to 20 November, leaving two earlier workouts unresolved.
bugs.expected: Only the two uncovered workouts are due; held workouts do not penalize the rate.
bugs.actual: Progress counted covered paused workouts, unlike the program and coach overview.
bugs.root: ProgressController omitted the shared availableOnSchedule scope.
bugs.fix: Reuse that scope in the existing monthly query.

bugs.reproduction: Open the same active run in two tabs. Pause it in one, then press Start workout in the stale tab.
bugs.actual: Start silently refreshed state with no explanation.
bugs.root: The run page POST had no onError handler.
bugs.fix: Render returned errors in an alert directly below the header; clear errors on a new attempt.

bugs.reproduction: Complete a future program session early; open its History detail and change it back to Planned or Skipped.
bugs.expected: Land on a valid session detail after the status change.
bugs.actual: The redirect returned to a History URL that no longer qualified, producing 404.
bugs.root: The status endpoint always redirected back despite changing History eligibility.
bugs.fix: Use the existing History scope to redirect to Calendar session detail only when that History URL is no longer eligible. Existing date filters and future simple-plan visibility are preserved.

ux.problem: Solid red End appeared above Start; Resume was secondary. The destructive action dominated the next useful action.
ux.fix: Place the next workout first; make Resume primary; make End a separated secondary action with the existing confirmation preview.
ux.verification: Visual before/after inspection and real lifecycle assertions in both engines.

ux.problem: Paused state hid the logical week in the header and suppressed an earlier workout even when its date was before the future pause boundary.
ux.fix: Show status, week and block together. Return the existing hold decision with next_workout and show eligible pre-pause work. Clarify pause-boundary wording.
ux.verification: Backend hold-boundary regression and browser checks at all seven widths.

architecture.finding: Read-only program lists imported a status formatter from the mutation modal.
architecture.action: Move the formatter to existing ProgramUI. No new component layer.

architecture.finding: Repeated permission lookups and nested snapshot queries grew from 141 to 1,437 HTTP queries for 12 versus 156 workouts.
architecture.action: Reuse freshly authorized assignment/subscription data within a review; centralize session eligibility in CoachAccess; eager-load the locked definition tree and batch update reads. Both sizes now use 34 HTTP queries.

architecture.finding: Progress used a separate due-session query without the existing hold scope.
architecture.action: Use availableOnSchedule consistently. ProgramLifecycle remains the logical-week/completion/adherence authority.

debt.problem: Library choice, custom media and nested superset-partner editing share a sizable stateful feature.
debt.risk: Future editor changes could regress nested focus or draft preservation.
debt.deferred: Current behavior and keyboard restoration pass; splitting state ownership now would add stabilization risk.
debt.direction: When changing partner editing, extract that meaningful flow with existing behavior tests; avoid tiny markup-only components.

debt.problem: The original global stylesheet remains large and mobile rules override some base selectors.
debt.risk: Future broad selectors can unintentionally affect unrelated features.
debt.deferred: No conflicting rule requiring a broad rewrite was reproduced; mobile regressions pass.
debt.direction: Move cohesive feature rules only when touching that feature, keeping shared tokens and mobile precedence explicit.

debt.problem: Each displayed run is synchronized and its position read; work is bounded by six cards or twelve rows but repeats reads per run.
debt.risk: Larger accounts can make these pages slower; current measured timings remain acceptable.
debt.deferred: Combining synchronization with list reads changes transaction/locking behavior. The per-workout query explosion was fixed separately.
debt.direction: If measured latency grows, return a synchronized position once per run or batch the read side while preserving row-lock and reopening tests.

limitations: Physical devices and screen readers not certified.
Production deployment and production smoke checks intentionally not performed.
Browser fixture creation/reset ordering corrected during test development; only successful final runs are counted.
